objective: Re-review (logic and edge cases only) of the "Water Born" audio mastering fix. …
objectiveFull: Re-review (logic and edge cases only) of the "Water Born" audio mastering fix. Context: scripts/master-audio.ts builds public/audio/ from paid originals in audio-src/. Intent: loops and music get ONE static gain toward a LUFS target, capped so true peak stays at or below -1 dBTP, with no dynamic processing so seamless loops stay seamless; narration and one-shot SFX (often boosted up to +20 dB) get the static gain plus an alimiter with latency=true (delay-compensated). Narration timing JSON maps ElevenLabs alignment onto each block's verbatim text. Verify the fix of the previous major finding (alimiter default latency=false delayed output 5 ms and was dynamic on loops) is correct and complete, and look for new logic errors in the changed lines (peak parsing incl. -inf, gain clamping order, which files are treated as static-only). Already dispositioned and NOT to be re-raised: write order of alignment vs mp3 in gen-audio.ts (rejected), duplicated buildNarrationInput call in two scripts (rejected), readdirSync id derivation and loop narrowing style (rejected), UTF-16 offset assumption (rejected, text is ASCII and mismatch throws), quiet count-chime (accepted). Mastered durations were checked equal to sources (fire-loop 20.000/20.000, p02 9.84/9.84).

findings.issue: The -1 dBTP cap uses the source's true peak (reported at 0.1 dB precision), and the gain is rounded with toFixed(2) before the 128k MP3 re-encode. Those steps plus encoder overshoot can put a capped file's final true peak slightly above -1 dBTP, still below 0 dBFS.
findings.fix: No change recommended; the -1 dB ceiling exists to absorb encoder overshoot. If a strict output guarantee is ever needed, measure the encoded output instead of the source.
